title: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO. Why Can One Job Move a Stock 31%?
fb_caption: Nvidia said on Monday, November 23 that its board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, eleven days after he resigned. The shares closed up more than 31% that day, adding nearly $1 trillion in market value, according to Reuters and CNBC. Nvidia also said an investigation by independent directors will continue. So why can one job move a giant company's value so much? Three big reasons: share prices are bets on the future, markets dislike uncertainty, and a board vote settles who is in charge. This is an explainer, not financial advice. Should one person matter this much to a company?
engagement_comment: Quick poll: how much should one CEO matter to a company's value? 1 = a lot, 2 = somewhat, 3 = hardly at all. Reply with a number!

beats.text: Nvidia says its board has voted to bring Jensen Huang back as chief executive, eleven days after he resigned. On Monday, November 23, the shares closed up more than 31 percent, according to Reuters and CNBC.
So why can one job move a giant company's value that much? Here are the three big reasons.

overlays.text:
WHY DOES ONE JOB
MOVE A STOCK?

beats.text: One: a share price is a bet on the future. Investors are usually not paying for last year's profits. They are paying for what they expect next. Change the person steering, and those expectations can change overnight.

items: A SHARE PRICE IS A BET ON THE FUTURE
PAYING FOR WHAT THEY EXPECT NEXT

beats.text: Two: markets dislike uncertainty. An empty top job leaves open questions. Who decides? Does the strategy change? Often, investors demand a lower price until they get answers.

items: OFTEN: A LOWER PRICE UNTIL ANSWERS

beats.text: Three: the board. Shareholders elect directors, and the directors hire and can remove the chief executive. So a board vote is usually the moment a leadership question gets a clear answer.

items: DIRECTORS HIRE, CAN REMOVE THE CEO
A BOARD VOTE = A CLEAR ANSWER

beats.text: Think of a huge ship in the middle of the ocean. Same engine. Same crew. Same cargo. But passengers feel very different when nobody knows who the captain is.

items: SAME ENGINE, SAME CREW, SAME CARGO
NOBODY KNOWS WHO THE CAPTAIN IS

beats.text: And size multiplies everything. Reuters reported the jump added nearly one trillion dollars in market value in a single day. It is not the end of the story. Nvidia said an investigation by independent directors will continue.

overlays.sub: MARKET VALUE ADDED IN ONE DAY (REUTERS)

items: NOT THE END OF THE STORY

beats.text: Takeaway: a share price is not just a score for products sold. It is a measure of confidence, and leadership is a big part of that. And confidence can swing both ways.

items: NOT JUST A SCORE FOR PRODUCTS SOLD
